newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines urged to keep stake in steel firm.
newsitem.headline: Philippines urged to keep stake in steel firm.

text.p: A senior officer of the Philippines' National Steel Corp (NSC) has urged the government to keep its stake in the steel-making firm after an attempt to auction its shares failed to attract bids.
"We would prefer the government to remain a shareholder of NSC. Steel is a very strategic and vital industry," NSC vice-chairman and chief executive Edgardo Espiritu said at the weekend.

Malaysia's Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd has bought a 75 percent stake in NSC. The remaining 25 percent is still in the hands of the Philippine government through the state-controlled National Development Co (NDC).
NDC had offered 20 percent of its stake for a minimum price of 10 pesos per share but none of 12 companies which earlier expressed interest offered bids at an auction last week.

Espiritu said NSC officials were not surprised at the failure of the bidding. "We expected that from the very start," he told reporters. "The 20 percent is too small to give any investor control of the firm."
An NDC official has said the auction probably failed because the investment involved was too high for a minority stake in the company.
Espiritu said the ideal scenario was for the government to maintain a 20 percent stake and offer its remaining five percent to small investors through an initial public offering.
He said this would depend on the NDC and the state committee on privatisation and he expected a decision on the matter next month.
